title: Wonder Is a Glitch
evidence_boundary: The 'stamp,' the peeling label, and the hand-as-object are metaphors for two real, well-documented perceptual effects: jamais vu and semantic satiation. The video does not claim reality is illusory — only that familiarity is a predictive overlay the brain adds, and that overlay can briefly wear thin.
desired_movement: From treating wonder as something rare or purchased, to recognizing it as a perceptual glitch the viewer can trigger deliberately.
grounding: The script keeps returning to the viewer's own name, hand, kitchen, and chair before the final invitation.
invitation: Look at your own hand until it turns back into an object.
end_card_question: What else have you stopped seeing just because it's familiar?
voice_standard: Liam — warm, sly, delighted by the idea, quick with the playful lines and mock-serious on the 'known, known, known' stamp beat, then intimate and spacious through the hand and the turn. A brilliant friend handing you a trick, not a solemn narrator. Drop nearly to a whisper on the final invitation.

scenes.text: Say your own name. Out loud. Now say it again — and again — thirty times, until your tongue starts tripping over it.
scenes.image_prompt: cinematic photoreal, a glowing wavelength of a spoken name, shallow depth of field, restrained practical lighting, muted filmic grade, subtle grain
scenes.symbol_query: a glowing wavelength of a spoken name

scenes.text: Somewhere around the twentieth, something goes sideways. The name stops being yours. It's just a sound. A little noise your mouth makes.
scenes.image_prompt: cinematic photoreal, a sound dissolving into slow ripples, shallow depth of field, restrained practical lighting, muted filmic grade, subtle grain
scenes.symbol_query: a sound dissolving into slow ripples

scenes.text: That's not you losing it. That's a glitch with a name. Jamais vu — the opposite of deja vu. Instead of the strange feeling familiar, the familiar goes strange.
scenes.image_prompt: cinematic photoreal, a looking glass reflection quietly reversing, shallow depth of field, restrained practical lighting, muted filmic grade, subtle grain
scenes.symbol_query: a looking glass reflection quietly reversing

scenes.text: Your brain runs on a stamp. A little rubber stamp that hits every face, every word, every object, and goes: known, known, known. You never see the stamp. You only see the world it already approved.
scenes.primary_symbol: a stamp pressing a blank sheet
scenes.image_prompt: cinematic photoreal, an ink stamp tool pressing a blank sheet, shallow depth of field, restrained practical lighting, muted filmic grade, subtle grain
scenes.symbol_query: an ink stamp tool pressing a blank sheet

scenes.text: Semantic satiation is what happens when you wear that stamp out. Say a word enough times and the ink runs dry. The meaning peels off the sound like a label off a bottle.
scenes.primary_symbol: a label lifting off a jar
scenes.image_prompt: cinematic photoreal, a paper label unfolding and lifting off a glass jar, shallow depth of field, restrained practical lighting, muted filmic grade, subtle grain
scenes.symbol_query: a paper label unfolding and lifting off a glass jar

scenes.text: And underneath the label? The raw thing. The actual noise. The strangeness that was sitting there the whole time — just covered.
scenes.image_prompt: cinematic photoreal, raw soil and root texture seen in macro, shallow depth of field, restrained practical lighting, muted filmic grade, subtle grain
scenes.symbol_query: raw soil and root texture seen in macro

scenes.text: You can do it with your own hand. Look at it. Really look. Past 'my hand' into the thing itself — five soft hooks, wet joints, a fold that opens and closes. Stare long enough and it becomes an object you happen to be wearing.
scenes.semantic_anchor: hand the test to the body
scenes.visual_function: hand the test to the body
scenes.image_prompt: cinematic photoreal, an open human hand turning into an unfamiliar object, shallow depth of field, restrained practical lighting, muted filmic grade, subtle grain
scenes.symbol_query: an open human hand turning into an unfamiliar object

scenes.text: It's a small vertigo, isn't it? The floor of the ordinary drops out. And for one second you're a stranger in your own kitchen, holding a fork you've never seen before.
scenes.image_prompt: cinematic photoreal, an ordinary kitchen room with a window, uncanny, shallow depth of field, restrained practical lighting, muted filmic grade, subtle grain
scenes.symbol_query: an ordinary kitchen room with a window, uncanny

scenes.text: Here's the part I love. People spend real money chasing this feeling. The world made new, the veil lifted. And it was free the whole time — built right into the hardware.
scenes.image_prompt: cinematic photoreal, an airport gate signpost and corridor at night, shallow depth of field, restrained practical lighting, muted filmic grade, subtle grain
scenes.symbol_query: an airport gate signpost and corridor at night

scenes.text: Because the familiarity was never in the thing. It was in you — a habit of prediction laid over the top so smoothly you mistook it for the world.
scenes.image_prompt: cinematic photoreal, a translucent veil and haze over an ordinary street, shallow depth of field, restrained practical lighting, muted filmic grade, subtle grain
scenes.symbol_query: a translucent veil and haze over an ordinary street

scenes.text: The word didn't change. Your hand didn't change. The stamp just skipped — and for a moment you saw what's always underneath: a universe that never actually agreed to be ordinary.
scenes.primary_symbol: the ordinary opening into a galaxy
scenes.image_prompt: cinematic photoreal, an ordinary street dissolving into a vast galaxy, shallow depth of field, restrained practical lighting, muted filmic grade, subtle grain
scenes.symbol_query: an ordinary street dissolving into a vast galaxy

scenes.text: Wonder isn't a place you have to travel to. It's a glitch. And you can trigger it on purpose — in a chair, with a single word.
scenes.image_prompt: cinematic photoreal, an empty chair by a bright window in a quiet room, shallow depth of field, restrained practical lighting, muted filmic grade, subtle grain
scenes.symbol_query: an empty chair by a bright window in a quiet room

scenes.text: So here's the test. Look at your own hand until it turns back into an object. That astonishment — it was always available. You just never stared long enough to be surprised.
scenes.image_prompt: cinematic photoreal, an afternoon sun ray moving across an open hand, shallow depth of field, restrained practical lighting, muted filmic grade, subtle grain
scenes.symbol_query: an afternoon sun ray moving across an open hand
